talk_track: Daniel Kirichanski here — I ran platform engineering at Ripple behind 6B+ annual transactions and PayPal's CI/CD platform for 9,000 developers, so the sentence in your Staff Engineer posting landed with me: "increasing complexity across payments, accounting, and ops. We need someone who can turn that into a durable, scalable system." Put that next to the Founding Engineer role asking one person to "help lead our existing engineering team of 5+ in India" and seed NYC from scratch, and it reads less like two hires than one architecture decision waiting on whoever arrives first. In money movement the thing that breaks at this point is rarely the code — it's the delivery system underneath it: deploy cadence, on-call, and a cost-to-serve you can't yet see per customer. At Ripple that's exactly where $8M of annual spend was hiding, and cutting it turned out to be the same work as getting deploys from hours to minutes. Whoever takes the role inherits that either way, so it's worth deciding before they start. Is the NYC-versus-India ownership split settled yet?
